extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors, journal editors, and peer reviewers in psychiatry/medical research
extracted.subtask_description: Content analysis of reasons why manuscripts were rejected at a specialty psychiatry journal, with guidance for authors, reviewers, and editors on common flaws and how to avoid them. Focuses on desk rejections, post-peer-review rejections, and post-editorial-re-review rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of novelty/originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript perceived to lack sufficient novelty or originality; the most common reason for desk rejection (≈51.8% of desk rejections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judgement of novelty has subjectivity but authors can increase perceived novelty by identifying limitations in previous papers and designing the study to address them; explicitly argue how your study advances prior work. Editors frequently desk-reject for perceived low scientific advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out of scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic or manuscript content falls outside the journal’s stated aims/scope; a common desk-rejection reason (17.4% of desk rejections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check journal scope and title carefully before submission. Selecting an inappropriate journal increases probability of quick desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design flaws (improper study design for the stated objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using an inappropriate study design for the research question (e.g., cross-sectional designs used to make causal inferences); classified as a fatal flaw central to study validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure study design matches the stated objectives; reframe objectives or choose appropriate design. Fatal design errors cannot be corrected at the review stage and are common grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of control group
rubrics_metrics.description: Absence of an appropriate control/comparison group when the research question requires one (listed as a sub-item under design flaws).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include or justify control groups where necessary; lack of an appropriate control is a serious methodological limitation that may require redesign of the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor control of confounders
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to measure or adjust for important confounding variables affecting the outcome (listed under design flaws/measurement errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan measurement and analyses to identify and control confounders (design, measurement, statistical adjustment). Lack of control is a fatal or serious flaw depending on context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obsolete or weak methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of outdated, weak, or inappropriate methods for the research question (part of design flaws).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contemporary, validated methods appropriate to the question; justify methodological choices and their limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak study rationale / poor justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient theoretical or empirical rationale for the study question; paper fails to convincingly argue why the study is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build a clear rationale referencing gaps in literature; explain how the study addresses limitations of prior work. Weak rationale often leads to rejection at peer-review/editorial stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing errors in the research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors in how the research question is framed that undermine the study’s focus or validity (identified as a 'fatal' flaw class).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate precise, answerable research questions aligned with design and analyses; consult mentors or methodologists early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics-related errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical deficiencies such as lack of informed consent/assent, missing Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC) approval, plagiarism, absence of trial registration (CTRI) for intervention trials, or duplicate submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and document IEC approval and informed consent as required; register clinical trials where applicable; avoid plagiarism and simultaneous submissions. Ethical lapses are serious grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism identified in the manuscript (listed under ethics-related errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure originality, proper citation, and use plagiarism-detection tools prior to submission. Plagiarism can lead to rejection and further sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No CTRI registration (for intervention trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to register intervention trials in the Clinical Trials Registry of India when applicable (CTRI omission listed among ethics reasons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register trials prospectively in appropriate registries and include registration details in the manuscript; lack of registration is a common regulatory/ethical rejection reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting the same manuscript to multiple journals or prior publication of the same work (listed under ethics errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit to one journal at a time and declare prior publications/overlapping submissions; duplicate submission risks desk rejection and ethical action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor elaboration of methods / inadequate methods description
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient description/detail of methodology, limiting reproducibility and assessment of rigor; most common issue at peer-review/editorial stages (e.g., 50.7% post-peer-review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, complete methods (design, sampling, instruments, procedures, analysis plan) and follow relevant reporting guidelines; reviewers frequently request improved methodological detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor writing / poor presentation / unintelligible language
rubrics_metrics.description: Low quality writing, poor organization, or language issues that hinder comprehension (a major reason for post-peer-review and editorial re-review rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in clear, concise, grammatically correct writing; seek senior-colleague input or professional editing. Poor presentation is often fixable but may still prompt rejection if severe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor presentation of results / repetition and inadequate discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Results presented poorly (e.g., repetition), and discussion inadequate (not covering recent evidence or synthesizing findings); common peer-review rejection reasons (inadequate discussion noted in 30.4% post-peer-review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present results clearly (tables/figures as appropriate), avoid unnecessary repetition, and write a critical, up-to-date discussion that situates findings within the literature and acknowledges limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement errors / incorrect choice of instruments or measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of inappropriate, invalid, or poorly selected measurement instruments; improper inclusion/exclusion criteria linked to measurement problems (commonly cited in post-publication letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose validated instruments suited to your population and objectives; justify choices and report psychometric properties or prior validation when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in data analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical mistakes such as improper tests for stated objectives, failure to correct for multiple comparisons, or other analytical errors (explicit sub-items and frequent in post-peer-review and letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan analyses consistent with study design and objectives, consult a statistician early, correct for multiple comparisons where appropriate, and report analyses transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrong conclusions / overstating results
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing conclusions not supported by the data or overstating findings; frequently cited at peer-review and editorial stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align conclusions strictly with results, acknowledge limitations, avoid causal claims from non-causal designs, and temper claims to what data support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small sample size / power issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Inadequate sample size or power calculations leading to underpowered studies (listed among desk reasons and post-publication letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform and report sample size/power calculations during planning; discuss implications of limited power and interpret null results cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor quality review articles (narrative when systematic needed; poor synthesis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review submissions that are non-systematic, lack adequate literature survey, or fail to synthesize findings critically; narrative reviews sometimes inappropriate when a systematic review is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate review type; for topics requiring comprehensive evidence synthesis, conduct a systematic review following standards; clearly describe search strategy and critical appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestions for technical modifications not followed
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors fail to implement requested technical modifications despite reminders (noted as a reason for rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to technical modification requests promptly and thoroughly; failure to follow required modifications can lead to rejection without peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection due to delayed revisions by authors / data recency concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts rejected because authors delayed revisions excessively, causing concerns about recency of data or relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address revisions promptly; long delays may lead editors to reject on grounds of loss of timeliness or changed editorial priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement for letters commenting on published articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters commenting on published articles were required to be submitted within a short window (e.g., within two months) and late submissions were rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe journal-specific time windows for post-publication comments; check submission policies for letters and rapid communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fatal versus non-fatal flaws (classification guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between fatal flaws (central to study validity: framing, design, instruments, ethics) and not-so-fatal flaws (fixable at revision: writing, analyses, multiple comparisons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize avoiding or addressing fatal flaws during study planning; many review-stage problems can be fixed, but design and ethical flaws often cannot—plan studies carefully to avoid irreversible problems.
